I'M SHANTANU
about.subtitle: Generalist Game Programmer
paragraphs: I have been playing video games for as long as I can remember. Eventually, just playing them wasn't enough so I wanted to know how they were made. That curiosity turned into a career, and I have been hooked on game development ever since.

I have over three years of experience working with Unity and C#, with the last two years spent professionally developing and shipping titles. As a generalist, I love getting my hands in every part of the engine. My work ranges from rapid R&D prototyping and programming core gameplay, to hooking up animations and audio, all the way to building full multiplayer architectures with custom matchmaking, leaderboards, and web APIs.

Whether I am participating in a weekend game jam to test out a weird new idea, learning a new tool, or collaborating with artists to polish a mechanic, I just genuinely love making games. I am always eager to solve interesting technical problems and help teams bring fun experiences to life.

projects.title: Real-Time Multiplayer Hand Cricket
projects.description: Performance-optimized up to 5v5 team-based multiplayer game utilizing Unity Netcode, Relay, and Lobby services with custom RPCs and cross-platform Android/WebGL simulation.
bodyParagraphs: Building a real-time multiplayer game that fits into a 34MB APK required strict asset management and highly optimized network traffic. I utilized Unity Netcode for GameObjects (NGO) alongside Unity Relay to bypass strict NAT punch-through issues on mobile networks.
To handle the 5v5 matchmaking, I integrated Unity Lobby. State synchronization is kept minimal, only passing enum states and compressed integers via custom RPCs, rather than heavy transform data.

One of the biggest hurdles was ensuring WebGL and Android clients stayed perfectly synchronized despite frame-rate discrepancies, which was solved by decoupling the game logic tick rate from the rendering framerate.

projects.title: State-Based 2D Boss Fight
projects.description: Modular boss AI designed using Finite State Machines to manage complex behavior transitions, attack patterns, and animation events across multiple combat phases.
bodyParagraphs: To make the boss encounter feel dynamic and readable, I engineered a modular Finite State Machine (FSM) architecture. Instead of massive update loops, each behavior (Idle, Dash, AOE_Attack) is encapsulated in its own state class.

Transitions between states are driven by distance checks and health thresholds. Furthermore, I tied hitbox activations directly to Animation Events, ensuring the damage frames perfectly sync with the visual swing of the weapon.

projects.title: Infinite Runner with Custom Shader
projects.description: Custom vertex shader simulating world curvature with procedural environment generation and multi-character selection featuring seamless restart logic.
bodyParagraphs: Instead of physically bending the level geometry, I wrote a custom HLSL vertex shader that offsets the Y-axis of vertices based on their Z-distance from the camera. This creates an 'Animal Crossing' style world curvature while maintaining flat physics colliders for precise platforming.
The procedural generation uses an object pool of track segments, seamlessly recycling them behind the camera and re-spawning them ahead to maintain a strict 60 FPS on lower-end mobile devices.

projects.title: Deterministic Rollback Netcode Prototype
projects.description: Lockstep rollback networking prototype built from scratch with fixed-point arithmetic, circular state history buffers, and bit-packed input delta compression.
bodyParagraphs: Standard floating-point math is non-deterministic across different CPUs, which breaks rollback networking. I wrote a custom fixed-point math library to ensure 100% deterministic physics simulations.

Inputs are bit-packed into lightweight integers and sent over UDP. If a packet is dropped, the system utilizes circular state history buffers to rewind the simulation, apply the delayed input, and fast-forward back to the current frame in a single tick.

projects.title: Runtime Memory Profiler & Object Pooler
projects.description: Lightweight in-engine memory allocation auditor and generic multi-tier pool manager eliminating GC spikes across scene streaming cycles.
